title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the combinatorics of the boundary ('structure à l'infini') of the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν}. A 'singularité' is a modular graph G' = (G', I' → S' →g' N). Here G' = (S', Ã', σ, o) is a graph presented by half-edges: S' are the vertices, Ã' the half-edges, σ the involution pairing half-edges into edges A' = Ã'/σ, and o the origin map Ã' → S'. I' → S' gives the marked points (legs) and g' gives the vertex genera. An 'MD-graphe' (Mumford–Deligne) is a connected modular graph satisfying the stability ('rigidité') inequality 2g_β + card I_β + card Ã_β ≥ 3 at every vertex. This is exactly the dual-graph condition for stable curves.

The page finishes a verification begun on the previous page. Given a set C' ⊂ A' of edges, one contracts them. The vertices α of the new graph G are the connected components of the subgraph (S', C'). For each α there is a vertex-graph G'(α). Its underlying graph is that component. Its markings are I'_α ⊔ B̃'_α, where B̃' = Ã' \ C̃' are the non-contracted half-edges with origin in S'_α.

One must show G is stable. By the proposition of n°3, if G'(α) is an MD-graph then its modular type (g_α, ν̂_α) is anabelian (2g_α − 2 + ν̂_α > 0). That is exactly the stability inequality at the vertex α of G.

Stability of G'(α) at β ∈ S'_α reads 2g'_β + (card I'_β + card B̃'_β) + card C̃'_β ≥ 3. The bracketed term is the 'marked weight' and the last term the 'order' (valence) of β in G'(α). Since Ã' = B̃' ⊔ C̃', this is literally 2g'_β + card I'_β + card Ã'_β ≥ 3, the MD condition for G' at β. Hence G'(α) is stable iff G' is stable at the vertices of S'_α.

Grothendieck then summarizes as a Proposition. For a singularity G' and a set of edges C', there exists, uniquely up to unique isomorphism, a generization morphism of singularities G' → G contracting exactly C'. The continuation on the next page says that π0 is preserved and that G' is stable iff all G'(α) are. In that case G is also stable.

In modern terms: edge contraction of stable graphs yields stable graphs. This is the specialization order on boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n}, i.e. the morphisms of the category of stable graphs underlying modular operads.
errors: No mathematical error. The equivalence is a tautological re-bracketing using Ã' = B̃' ⊔ C̃'.
In the second inequality the half-edge set should carry a prime (Ã'_β, not Ã_β).

The genus formula for the contracted vertex (sum of the g'_β plus the first Betti number of the component) is not on this page. It must be supplied for (g_α, ν̂_α) to be the modular type of G'(α). It is presumably on the previous or next pages.

ideas.what: Encoding modular (dual) graphs of stable pointed curves via half-edges with involution σ and origin map, plus genus function and legs
ideas.modern_name: stable graphs / modular graphs (Getzler–Kapranov, Kontsevich–Manin formalism of flags/half-edges)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen 1983; half-edge formalism popularized by Kontsevich–Manin 1994, Getzler–Kapranov 1998
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse d'un programme in this explicit form (only the 'structure à l'infini' of the Teichmüller tower is discussed there)

ideas.what: Stability ('rigidité MD') condition 2g_β + card I_β + valence ≥ 3 at each vertex, and the link with anabelian type 2g − 2 + ν > 0
ideas.modern_name: stability of a genus-n-pointed graph; hyperbolicity of (g,ν)
ideas.where_published: The term 'anabélien' for hyperbolic types appears in Esquisse / the letter to Faltings, but not this graph lemma

ideas.what: Contraction of a set of edges as a 'morphisme de générisation de singularités', unique up to unique isomorphism, preserving connectedness and stability
ideas.modern_name: edge contraction in the category of stable graphs; specialization order of boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore since Deligne–Mumford/Knudsen; formalized by Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine verification that contracting edges of a stable graph yields a stable graph, a standard fact in the stratification of \bar M_{g,n}. It is historically mildly interesting as an early half-edge formalism and as Grothendieck's own 'générisation' terminology, but nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The insertion before 'MD sur G'' appears to read 'de rigidité', not 'de stabilité'. This is consistent with 'condition de rigidité MD' on the next page.
'soit C' ⊂ A' ... une union d'orbites de G'' more plausibly reads 'un ens[emble] d'arêtes de G''. C' is a subset of the edge set A'.
The labels under the braces are 'poids marqué de β dans G(α)' and 'ordre de β dans G(α)'. In the second formula they read 'poids marqué de β dans G'' and 'ordre de β dans G''.
